meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, come on, Dad!
Well?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'too, also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Me too.
He's here too.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

подходить.gloss: to approach, to come up; to suit

meanings.en: to approach, to come up; to suit
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to approach, to come up; to suit', paired with 'подойти'.

examples.trans: Let's go, our turn in the queue is coming up.
The train is approaching the station.

examples.text: Я к печке подхожу. А он маячит перед глазами!
examples.trans: I walk up to the stove. And it dangles right before my eyes!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'all right, OK', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go.
OK, I'm coming.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
That's it, bye!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'they', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They are building a centre.
History will punish them.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'рядок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order.
Everything is in complete order.

examples.text: Теперь давай всё по порядку. Скажи мне, сколько ты им должна?
examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order. Tell me, how much do you owe them?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Where's my toy car?
Where's Dad?

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'because of; from behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'whether, if; (что ли) or what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Did you forget, or what?
I don't know whether he is at home.
Was it Osipenko who hired you?

подраться.gloss: to fight, have a brawl, scuffle

meanings.en: to fight, have a brawl, scuffle
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'раться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fight, have a brawl, scuffle', paired with 'драться'.

examples.trans: The men had a fierce fight in the courtyard.
The boys fought over the ball.
Your dad had a big fight again.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is this?
He's so kind.
Pavel Yuryevich, what is this?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
But you've still got some.
I told you: no.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'let's go'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?
Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.
All right, let's go to our room.

meanings.note: Common Russian noun meaning 'tea' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Now I'll make some tea too.
Would you like a cup of tea?

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to drink', paired with 'выпить'.

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

examples.trans: I'm drinking tea.
He doesn't drink.

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give; (imperative) let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.trans: Let's talk.
He gives me a book.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

раздеваться.gloss: to take off one's coat; to undress

meanings.en: to take off one's coat; to undress
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'деваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take off one's coat; to undress', paired with 'раздеться'.

examples.trans: Don't, don't take your coat off!
Come in and take off your coat.

examples.text: Но сейчас не время. Не надо, не раздевайся!
examples.trans: But now isn't the time. Don't, don't take your coat off!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, get ready', paired with 'готовиться'.

examples.trans: Get ready for the procedure.
We got ready to go out.
Arkady Borisovich, prepare for the procedure.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пециально'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Are you doing this on purpose?
Are you doing this on purpose or what?
You left it here on purpose.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучай'). Common masculine noun meaning 'case, occasion, incident' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Take it, just in case.
This is a strange case.

examples.text: Возьмите, пожалуйста. На случай, если передумаете.
examples.trans: Please take this. In case you change your mind.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be stored, kept'.

related.gloss: not to to be stored (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Специально для такого случая у нас хранится кое-что.
examples.trans: We have something saved specially for an occasion like this.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет храниться без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to be stored without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something, a thing or two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And one more thing.
I want to show you something.

examples.text: И ещё кое-что. Эдуард Владимирович просил передать привет.
examples.trans: And one more thing. Eduard Vladimirovich asked us to pass on his regards.
